decisions.reason: Having remained on the market after launch, the combined shuttering and de-shuttering robot is deeply rooted in the firm's core automation, formwork and control knowledge, so absorptive capacity favors further refinement over withdrawal.

The automatic de-shuttering robot is closely tied to established precast process expertise and can be improved through learning from installed plants, though some functional overlap with broader robotic solutions keeps a modest exit risk.

The profile storage robot still fits the firm's production-system capabilities and broad plant offering, but as a more specialized module it remains somewhat more exposed if customer demand stays niche.
The automatic shuttering robot matches the firm's long-developed system integration and in-house R&D strengths, making continued commercialization more likely than discontinuation.

The combined magazining cleaning and plotting machine builds directly on the firm's plant-equipment know-how and, as a product line with several models, offers scope to adapt variants rather than abandon the line quickly.

Production analysis software is close to the firm's controls, consulting and lifecycle-support capabilities, so the firm has the absorptive capacity to iterate it, although software adoption and integration risks are slightly higher than for core machinery.
